the joints are feasible, the joint design is robust and the joint performance is satisfactory

(1) the joint design, based on the use of an intermediate layer of a copper alloy (CuCrZr) between two superconducting layers, is feasible and can be used for the manufacture of the ITER conductor joints, (2) a joint design, based only on the use of a superconducting material (NbTi), is not feasible, and (3) the joint design based on the use a superconducting layer and a copper alloy (NbTi + CuCr
(1) a reliable joint can be designed and manufactured, (2) the joints can withstand the required operating stresses and (3) the joints do not significantly affect the performance of the conductors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of the joint and the development of manufacturing methods, with particular attention to the following issues: (1) the joint layout and the mechanical behaviour of the conductor in the joint; (2) the electrical and thermal performance of the joint; (3) the manufacturing methods and the joint assembly; (4) the joint performance in the test facilities.

the development of a reliable joint technology for the ITER conductor, which meets the stringent ITER requirements for joint electrical resistance, joint thermal conductivity, joint mechanical properties, and joint thermal stability.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the joint concept and the manufacturing process are well established, and the design criteria are well defined.
the design criteria and manufacturing processes for the ITER joint have been successfully established.

- the design and manufacturing of subsize and of full size joint samples have been carried out according to the agreed criteria; - the subsize joints have been tested successfully; - the full size joints have been tested in the PFT facility with a current density of 100 A/mm2; the results show that the joint resistance is in the range expected for the ITER design; - the full-size joints have been tested with a current density up to 200 A/mm2 in the SULTAN
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of the ITER conductor joint, based on the criteria and manufacturing choices agreed in the EDA, has been validated by test data obtained from subsize samples.
we have developed a joint technology which meets the ITER design requirements and which has been successfully tested in the PPF facility.

the design criteria and manufacturing methods for the joints are well established, the manufacturing methods have been developed, tested and validated and a full set of joint samples is available for performance testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ITER joint design is robust and reliable.

the design and the manufacturing choices for the ITER joint are robust, with respect to the variations of the layout parameters, and that the joint is able to withstand the ITER operating conditions without any degradation.
the ITER conductor joints can be manufactured in a way that is compatible with the ITER conductor manufacturing process.
